description: The plot illustrates how three accuracy measures (Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy) vary as a function of Initial Confidence. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.91 to 0.99 with tick labels at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with major ticks at 0.2 intervals. The Final Accuracy series is shown as a solid blue line with circular markers and vertical error bars; it stays high across the range, starting near 0.90 at 0.91, rising to about 0.98 at 0.93, dipping to about 0.86 at 0.96, and ending around 0.92 at 0.99. The Δ Accuracy series is shown as an orange dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars; it begins around 0.55 at 0.91, peaks near 0.67 at 0.92, declines to about 0.28 at 0.96, rises to about 0.46 at 0.97, drops to about 0.10 at 0.98, and ends near 0.15 at 0.99. The Initial Accuracy series is shown as a green dash-dot line with square markers and vertical error bars; it starts around 0.36 at 0.91, dips to about 0.27 at 0.92, increases to about 0.53 at 0.93, fluctuates around 0.48–0.59 from 0.94 to 0.96, drops to about 0.42 at 0.97, then rises sharply to about 0.87 at 0.98 and ends around 0.77 at 0.99.
